_comment: Context that lets every Go block in the docs parse on its own. Read by
scripts/check-examples.py. Blocks are keyed by (file, order, first non-blank
line): first_line must match the block exactly, so adding, moving, or editing
a block fails the check until this file is updated.
Extended shape: every block entry may carry first_line (required when an
entry exists) plus one of skip (reason string) or template (a list of
lines with {code} as the slot); a file entry may also carry a per-file
prelude. Blocks with no entry are auto-wrapped two ways and checked in
both forms: as `package p` + block (declaration shape) as well as
`package p` + `func _()` around the block (statement shape). A block
passes if either form parses, so ordinary fragments need no entry.
skip, with a reason, marks a block that cannot stand as syntax (a bare
signature, an elided body, two file excerpts in one fence, or the
domain-pure counterexample that shows the forbidden import on purpose).
Skipped blocks are exempt from the domain check, counted in the summary,
and never silently dropped.
Known exemption: only top-level ```go fences are blocks. A ```go fence
nested inside another fence (the ~~~markdown report template in
skills/go-review/SKILL.md carries one, holding a placeholder, not real
code) is not a block: it is not checked and not counted. Keep real Go
examples out of nested fences.
